question_text:
What is the composition, in weight percent, of an alloy that consists of 94.1 at $\% \mathrm{Ag}$ and 5.9 at $\% \mathrm{Cu}$ ? The atomic weights for Ag and Cu are $107.87 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ and $63.55 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$, respectively.

Give your answer as a tuple (the wight percent of Ag, the weight percent of Cu).The units of each required answer are (wt%, wt%), respectively.
response:
Converting atomic percent to weight percent. Take a basis of 100 atoms: 94.1 atoms Ag and 5.9 atoms Cu.

- Mass Ag = 94.1 × 107.87 = 10150.567 g
- Mass Cu = 5.9 × 63.55 = 374.945 g
- Total = 10525.512 g

$$w_{\mathrm{Ag}} = \frac{10150.567}{10525.512}\times 100 = 96.44\%$$
$$w_{\mathrm{Cu}} = \frac{374.945}{10525.512}\times 100 = 3.562\%$$

Sig-fig check: the limiting input is 5.9 (2 sig figs). Computing Cu to 2 sig figs gives 3.6 wt%; since Ag% = 100 − Cu% (addition rule, fixed to the same decimal place), Ag = 96.4 wt%. The pair sums to 100, consistent.

$$\boxed{(96.4,\ 3.6)}$$
